newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end mixed, T-bonds recover late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end mixed, T-bonds recover late.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed mixed, as T-bonds shrugged off the results of the U.S. Treasury's three-year note auction and recovered late, traders said.
"Locals had a chance to get a bearish signal in place, but couldn't do it," one bond futures trader said.
"A lower close would have told us a different story," he said, adding that a weak close would have established an outside down day and pointed to near term losses.
Locals were the primary sellers in the bond pit on news the auction produced a yield of 6.44 percent and a bid-to-cover of 2.08. June T-bonds fell below the 110-00 level.
June, which closed at 110-01/32 on Monday, steadily inched lower, as Eurodollars set daily lows on the heels of the sale results.
Dealers were aggressive sellers of Eurodollars, with one U.S. dealer alone selling 2,000 September. September immediately fell to 93.845, near support at 93.83.
On Wednesday, the Treasury will sell $12 10-year notes.
Aside from the bid-to-cover ratio, several traders in both the bond and Eurodollar pits described the auction as average.
"Yes, the bid-to-cover was low, but the non-comp bids were higher which means it was spread out and it wasn't concentrated in a few hands," one Eurodollar futures trader said.
Non-comp bids totaled $967 million, versus some market estimates of $700 million to $800 million.

September Eurodollars eased towards support at 93.83, but held above that level. Key support rests at 93.79 and at 93.54 for December. December becomes lead contract month on Thursday, the exchange said.
Some traders brushed aside June T-bonds' fall through 110-00, adding that the market has not seen the type of profit-taking that usually follows a sharp rally.
"The market just hasn't seen profit-taking, which is a good sign," one bond futures trader said.
"Given everything we've seen in the last few months, it's acting well," he said, adding that June T-bonds could test the two-month high of 110-14/32 in the near term.
On Wednesday, preliminary first-quarter productivity data and March wholesale inventory data will be released. In the afternoon, the Federal Reserve's Beige Book is scheduled for release.

At the close, June T-bonds were up 2/32 at 110-03/32, 10-year notes were flat at 107-09/32, muni-bonds rose 5/32 to 115-09/32, September T-bills fell 0.005 bp to 94.465, Eurodollars lost 0.015 to 93.870. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
